# Implementation-Readiness Checklist: Operator Code Console

**Purpose**: Review whether the Feature 011 requirements, plan, and contracts are sufficiently complete, unambiguous, measurable, and bounded to generate implementation tasks. This is a requirements-quality review, not a test of implementation.
**Created**: 2026-09-10
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md), [plan.md](../plan.md), and [contracts/](../contracts/)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` workflow from the approved Feature 011 context.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Do FR-001 through FR-003 state which shell traffic is forbidden, when a count may be authoritative, and when settings-owned data may begin loading?
- [ ] CHK002 Do FR-004 through FR-006 define the real BrowserSubject, exact Source/Checkout grant, immutable View, and independent browser/MCP contexts without role, Space, path, label, or tab-derived authority?
- [ ] CHK003 Do FR-007 and the HTTP contract distinguish ordinary binding/discovery/intent-admission authorization from contextual status, query, graph, source, continuation, and resulting-View release categories?
- [ ] CHK004 Does the browser-context contract name one authoritative binding transition table, including fresh opener normalization, duplicate collision, acknowledged and delayed reload, crash expiry, replay, and session/binding expiry outcomes?
- [ ] CHK005 Do FR-010 through FR-015 define the four selection forms, frozen-filter invalidation, the Rules-first action matrix, every later-domain matrix, and the exact twelve shared mutation-result callers?
- [ ] CHK006 Do FR-016 and FR-017 specify durable intent states, idempotency, daemon-only acknowledgement/execution, retry, terminal failure, and released resulting-View readback without browser filesystem or credential access?
- [ ] CHK007 Do FR-020 through FR-024 define one-way design promotion, all nine truthful UI states, localization/accessibility boundaries, honest Books legacy-import wording, and the prohibited Queue/S6 controls?
- [ ] CHK008 Does the mechanism-adaptation contract distinguish the bounded current-slice S2 gate from the separate R-C expansion gate, with no transferred benchmark, parity, or support claim?

## Requirement clarity and consistency

- [ ] CHK009 Is Source-owner issuance/revocation stated as exact principal equality in the same realm with transactional audit, and are disabled-auth, administrator, keycard, and implied-authority paths explicitly excluded?
- [ ] CHK010 Is every contextual request constrained to a selected Source, Checkout, and pinned immutable View, with an unambiguous fail-closed posture for missing, stale, revoked, or mismatched context?
- [ ] CHK011 Does `OperatorMutationResult` distinguish known commitment, failed verification, mixed outcomes, pre-effect failure, and unknown commitment without calling an optimistic reset a rollback?
- [ ] CHK012 Are selection tokens, continuations, operation statuses, and intents explicitly non-capabilities whose current authorization/version/context checks are named at execution or release?
- [ ] CHK013 Do the plan dependency graph, ordered slices, and ownership table agree that S1a precedes S1b; S2 and accepted Rules jointly admit Book planning; only full S2/S3/S4 completion admits Book implementation; and R-C expansion does not block bounded S2?
- [ ] CHK014 Do the exclusive-writer rules assign `service.go`, `migrations.go`, shared live-harness configuration/package script, `useOperatorApi.ts`, and localization/design surfaces to exactly one owner at a time?
- [ ] CHK015 Do scope exclusions consistently forbid UCI reacceptance, a second graph, direct storage, HTTP MCP, broad IAM, secrets, deployment/release, Book implementation, Memory R1 reprioritization, and S6 workflow expansion?

## Acceptance-quality and evidence coverage

- [ ] CHK016 Do SC-001, SC-009, SC-010, and SC-011 name observable traffic/state/accessibility/localization/legacy-capability evidence rather than mock-only interaction as connection proof?
- [ ] CHK017 Do SC-002 and SC-003 require a two-worktree, two-tab, concurrent-MCP fixture with same-View coherence and explicit non-disclosure for denial, revocation, ambiguity, expiry, replay, and continuation mismatch?
- [ ] CHK018 Do SC-004 through SC-006 name the >200 Rules and >100 Issues corpus, each selection form, authorization/version changes, per-item outcomes, retry limits, and all-or-none Rules reorder proof?
- [ ] CHK019 Do SC-007 and the intent contract require daemon acknowledgement plus an authorized readable resulting View before completion, while preserving truthful queued or unavailable offline states?
- [ ] CHK020 Does SC-008 require trigger-to-browser-request-to-handler-to-domain/UCI-to-observed-effect-or-readback evidence, and label mock browser tests only as interaction evidence?

## Scenario and non-functional coverage

- [ ] CHK021 Do the contracts make normal semantic readiness, lexical/degraded/unavailable presentation, bounded graph/partial coverage, exact stored-span reads, normal watcher reconciliation, A/B isolation, and explicit newer-View transition distinguishable?
- [ ] CHK022 Are keyboard selection, indeterminate header state, 1440/980/390 CSS-pixel widths, 200% zoom, RU/EN, zh regression, and the actions/limitations of all nine UI states measurable without treating `empty` as a denial or unavailable result?
- [ ] CHK023 Does the live-fixture boundary require a disposable PostgreSQL database, real authenticated Go server, real browser/linked worktrees/ordinary agent/MCP, grant issuance through the application, and no production data, disabled auth, direct grant row, or secret exposure?
- [ ] CHK024 Does the residual ledger identify the exact consumer tuple, provider readiness, watcher variance, target-profile restrictions, comparator disposition, and non-release Sonar boundary without converting a finite residual into new Feature 011 scope?

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit.implement` must not modify checklist markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` retains its separate specification-review lifecycle.
